New Delhi: The new All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) hospitals established under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY) have collectively recorded over six crore outpatient department (OPD) consultations in five years since 2021-22, as of October 31 this year.The achievement reflects the growing reach of these institutions and their contribution to bringing specialised tertiary healthcare services closer to people across the country, the ministry said.

The number of OPD consultations at these institutions has risen steadily, from 50.03 lakh in 2021-22 to 77.95 lakh in 2022-23, 100.52 lakh in 2023-24, 129.98 lakh in 2024-25 and 144.96 lakh in 2025-26, the ministry said in a statement.

Advt

During the current financial year, the new AIIMS hospitals recorded 97.41 lakh OPD consultations till October this year, it said.

Of the 22 new AIIMS hospitals approved under PMSSY in various phases, 18 are fully functional, providing services including outpatient and inpatient care, emergency and trauma services, diagnostics, medical education and research.The expansion of AIIMS under PMSSY is aimed at addressing regional disparities in the availability of affordable and reliable tertiary healthcare, while also strengthening medical education and research infrastructure, according to the ministry.

The new AIIMS hospitals have also expanded opportunities for undergraduate, postgraduate and nursing education and are developing specialised clinical facilities and advanced medical services.The growing OPD footfall reflects increased utilisation of specialised healthcare services and the expanding reach of these institutions across the country, the ministry said.
